25/G.goal: Explain why XR design depends on human perception and describe the perceptual-psychology and sensory-system foundations it relies on.
25/G.achieves: Provides the learner with the human-factors foundation needed to understand later XR perception topics and to design or evaluate XR systems more effectively.

25/O1.goal: Explain why XR interaction and perceptual design must account for human perception and why inconsistent virtual stimulation can produce adaptation or cybersickness.
25/O1.achieves: Gives the learner the human-factors rationale for studying presence, perceptual design, and cybersickness in XR systems.

25/O2.goal: Describe the perceptual-psychology and sensory basis of XR, including the human senses' stimuli, receptors, sense organs, and selective detection.
25/O2.achieves: Provides the physiological and perceptual foundation for later lectures on vision, auditory experience, balance, and other senses in XR.
